blocks.prompt: 1 (i) Find the values of \(x\) and \(y\): \(x + iy + 2 - 3i = i(5 - i)(3 + 4i)\).
blocks.explanation:
Dekhiye, yeh equality (barabri) wala sawal hai: bayen taraf ek complex number hai aur dayen taraf doosra, aur dono ko barabar kaha gaya hai.
Diya kya hai? Left side par \(x + iy + 2 - 3i\) aur right side par teen cheezon ka product \(i(5 - i)(3 + 4i)\).
Find kya karna hai? Do real numbers \(x\) aur \(y\).
Kaunsa rule? Equality of complex numbers: do complex numbers tabhi barabar hote hain jab un ke real parts bhi barabar hon aur imaginary parts bhi. Yahi rule do alag equations de dega.
Plan: pehle right side ko multiply kar ke seedha \(a + ib\) form mein layenge, phir left side ke real aur imaginary hisse alag karenge, aur aakhir mein dono parts ko aamne saamne rakh kar compare karenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(x + iy + 2 - 3i = i(5 - i)(3 + 4i)\), aur \(x, y\) real numbers hain.
Humein find karna hai: real numbers \(x\) aur \(y\).
Tareeqa: Equality of complex numbers: agar \(a + ib = c + id\) ho to \(a = c\) aur \(b = d\). Yeh rule yahan isliye fit hota hai kyunke simplify karne ke baad dono sides ek ek complex number ban jati hain, aur phir hum real ko real se aur imaginary ko imaginary se mila sakte hain. Is tarah ek equation se do equations mil jati hain, aur do unknowns ke liye do equations hi chahiye hoti hain.

Right side ke do brackets multiply karein
\[(5 - i)(3 + 4i)\]
\[= 15 + 20i - 3i - 4i^2\]
\[= 15 + 17i + 4\]
\[= 19 + 17i\]
Kyun: Teen cheezon ka product ek saath karna mushkil hai, is liye pehle do brackets ko multiply karte hain. Pehle bracket ka har term doosre bracket ke har term se multiply hota hai (jaise algebra mein \((a + b)(c + d)\) karte hain). \(20i - 3i = 17i\) like terms hain. Aur \(i^2 = -1\) hai, is liye \(-4i^2 = -4(-1) = +4\) ban jata hai jo real number hai aur 15 ke saath jur jata hai.
Dhyan dein: Bohat se students \(-4i^2\) ko \(-4\) likh dete hain. Yaad rakhiye, minus ko minus se multiply karein to plus banta hai.

Ab \(i\) se multiply karein
\[i(19 + 17i) = 19i + 17i^2\]
\[= 19i - 17\]
\[= -17 + 19i\]
Kyun: Bahar wala \(i\) bracket ke dono terms se multiply hota hai: \(i \cdot 19 = 19i\) aur \(i \cdot 17i = 17i^2 = -17\). Aakhir mein hum real part \(-17\) ko pehle likhte hain taake number standard \(a + ib\) form mein aa jaye; is form mein real aur imaginary part seedha nazar aate hain aur compare karna aasaan ho jata hai.

Left side ko group karein
\[x + iy + 2 - 3i\]
\[= (x + 2) + i(y - 3)\]
Kyun: Left side mein chaar terms bikhre hue hain. Kyunke \(x\) aur 2 dono real hain, in ko ek bracket mein rakha: \((x + 2)\) real part hai. \(iy\) aur \(-3i\) dono ke saath \(i\) hai, in se \(i\) common nikala: \(i(y - 3)\), to \(y - 3\) imaginary part hai. Yeh grouping isi liye zaroori hai ke left side bhi \(a + ib\) shakal mein aa jaye.

Real aur imaginary parts compare karein
\[(x + 2) + i(y - 3) = -17 + 19i\]
\[x + 2 = -17\]
\[x = -19\]
\[y - 3 = 19\]
\[y = 22\]
Kyun: Ab dono sides ek jaisi shakal mein hain. Equality of complex numbers ke mutabiq real part real part ke barabar: \(x + 2 = -17\), is liye \(x = -17 - 2 = -19\). Imaginary part imaginary part ke barabar: \(y - 3 = 19\), is liye \(y = 22\). Ek complex equation ne humein do aam linear equations de di hain.
Dhyan dein: Imaginary part \(19\) hai, \(19i\) nahi; \(i\) ko equation mein mat likhiye.

Tasdeeq: values wapas rakh kar dekhein
\[-19 + 22i + 2 - 3i\]
\[= -17 + 19i \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Achhe students hamesha jawab check karte hain. \(x = -19\) aur \(y = 22\) left side mein rakhne se \(-19 + 2 = -17\) aur \(22i - 3i = 19i\) mila, yani \(-17 + 19i\), jo bilkul right side hai. Is liye hamara jawab pakka sahi hai.
blocks.final_answer:
\(x = -19,\ y = 22\)
Yani left side mein yeh values rakhne se dono taraf ek hi complex number \(-17 + 19i\) ban jata hai.

blocks.prompt: 1 (ii) Find the values of \(x\) and \(y\): \((x + iy)(1 - i) = (2 - 3i)(-5 + 5i)(-i3/5)\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh bhi equality ka sawal hai, lekin is dafa \(x + iy\) akela nahi balkay \((1 - i)\) se multiply ho kar aaya hai.
Diya kya hai? Right side par teen factors ka product hai; kitab ka \((-i3/5)\) asal mein \(-\frac{3i}{5}\) hai.
Find kya karna hai? Real numbers \(x\) aur \(y\).
Rule kaunsa? Pehle \(x + iy\) ko akela karna hai, jis ke liye \(1 - i\) se divide karna parega. Complex number se divide karne ka tareeqa conjugate se multiply karna hai, kyunke is se denominator real ban jata hai.
Plan: right side simplify, phir conjugate ki madad se divide, aur aakhir mein parts compare.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \((x + iy)(1 - i) = (2 - 3i)(-5 + 5i)(-i3/5)\); \((-i3/5)\) ka matlab \(-\frac{3i}{5}\) hai.
Humein find karna hai: \(x\) aur \(y\).
Tareeqa: Pehle right side ke teen factors ka product nikalenge. Phir \(x + iy\) ko akela karne ke liye dono taraf \(1 - i\) se divide karenge. Divide karne ke liye upar neeche conjugate (ulta sign wala saathi) \(1 + i\) se multiply karte hain, kyunke \((1 - i)(1 + i)\) real number deta hai, aur real number se divide karna bilkul aasaan hai.

Right side ke pehle do factors multiply karein
\[(2 - 3i)(-5 + 5i)\]
\[= -10 + 10i + 15i - 15i^2\]
\[= -10 + 25i + 15\]
\[= 5 + 25i\]
Kyun: Har term ko har term se multiply kiya: \(2(-5) = -10\), \(2(5i) = 10i\), \((-3i)(-5) = 15i\), aur \((-3i)(5i) = -15i^2\). Kyunke \(i^2 = -1\), \(-15i^2 = +15\) real ho gaya aur \(-10\) ke saath mil kar 5 bana. \(10i + 15i = 25i\).
Dhyan dein: \((-3i)(-5)\) mein do minus milte hain to plus \(15i\) aata hai; yahan sign ki ghalti bohat aam hai.

Teesre factor se multiply karein
\[(5 + 25i)\left(-\dfrac{3i}{5}\right)\]
\[= -3i - 15i^2\]
\[= 15 - 3i\]
Kyun: \(-\frac{3i}{5}\) bracket ke dono terms se multiply hota hai: \(5 \times (-3i/5) = -3i\) (5 cancel ho gaya), aur \(25i \times (-3i/5) = -15i^2 = +15\). Real part pehle likha. Ab poora sawal itna simple ho gaya hai: \((x + iy)(1 - i) = 15 - 3i\).

\(1 - i\) se divide karein
\[x + iy = \dfrac{15 - 3i}{1 - i}\]
\[= \dfrac{(15 - 3i)(1 + i)}{(1 - i)(1 + i)}\]
Kyun: \(x + iy\) ko akela karne ke liye dono sides ko \(1 - i\) se divide kiya. Lekin denominator mein \(i\) ho to fraction ko \(a + ib\) mein nahi tor sakte. Is liye upar aur neeche dono ko conjugate \(1 + i\) se multiply kiya. Upar neeche ek hi cheez se multiply karna asal mein 1 se multiply karna hai, is liye value bilkul nahi badalti, sirf shakal badalti hai.
Dhyan dein: Conjugate mein sirf \(i\) wale part ka sign badalta hai: \(1 - i\) ka conjugate \(1 + i\) hai, \(-1 + i\) nahi.

Upar aur neeche simplify karein
\[(1 - i)(1 + i) = 1 - i^2 = 2\]
\[(15 - 3i)(1 + i)\]
\[= 15 + 15i - 3i - 3i^2\]
\[= 18 + 12i\]
\[x + iy = \dfrac{18 + 12i}{2}\]
\[= 9 + 6i\]
Kyun: Neeche \((a - b)(a + b) = a^2 - b^2\) wala formula laga: \(1 - i^2 = 1 - (-1) = 2\), jo real hai, yahi conjugate ka faida tha. Upar har term multiply kiya; \(-3i^2 = +3\) real ho kar 15 ke saath 18 bana, aur \(15i - 3i = 12i\). Phir dono parts ko 2 se divide kar diya.

Parts compare karein
\[x + iy = 9 + 6i\]
\[x = 9,\quad y = 6\]
Kyun: Ab left side \(x + iy\) aur right side \(9 + 6i\) dono \(a + ib\) shakal mein hain. Equality of complex numbers ke mutabiq real parts barabar (\(x = 9\)) aur imaginary parts barabar (\(y = 6\)).

Tasdeeq: wapas multiply karein
\[(9 + 6i)(1 - i)\]
\[= 9 - 9i + 6i - 6i^2\]
\[= 15 - 3i \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Asal equation mein \(x + iy\) ko \(1 - i\) se multiply kiya gaya tha, is liye check ke liye hum bhi \(9 + 6i\) ko \(1 - i\) se multiply karte hain. \(-6i^2 = +6\), to \(9 + 6 = 15\) aur \(-9i + 6i = -3i\). Wohi \(15 - 3i\) mila jo right side ka simplified form tha, is liye jawab sahi hai.
blocks.final_answer:
\(x = 9,\ y = 6\)
Yani \(x + iy = 9 + 6i\) hai, jo \(1 - i\) se multiply ho kar right side ka \(15 - 3i\) deta hai.

blocks.prompt: 1 (iii) Find the values of \(x\) and \(y\): \(\frac{x}{2 + i} + \frac{y}{3 - i} = 4 + 5i\).
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein \(x\) aur \(y\) fractions ke upar baithe hain aur neeche complex numbers hain.
Diya kya hai? Do fractions ka jama \(4 + 5i\) ke barabar hai.
Find kya karna hai? Real numbers \(x\) aur \(y\).
Rule kaunsa? Jab tak denominator mein \(i\) hai, real aur imaginary part alag nazar nahi aate. Is liye har fraction ko uske denominator ke conjugate se multiply kar ke rationalise (denominator ko real banana) karenge, phir equality of complex numbers lagayenge.
Plan: dono fractions rationalise, real aur imaginary parts ikatthe, compare kar ke do linear equations, aur unhein saath solve.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\frac{x}{2 + i} + \frac{y}{3 - i} = 4 + 5i\), \(x, y\) real hain.
Humein find karna hai: \(x\) aur \(y\).
Tareeqa: Har fraction ko uske denominator ke conjugate se upar neeche multiply karenge (rationalise karna), taake neeche real number aa jaye. Phir har fraction real part + imaginary part mein toot jayega. Equality of complex numbers se do simultaneous linear equations (aisi do equations jo saath saath solve hoti hain) milengi.

Pehla fraction rationalise karein
\[\dfrac{x}{2 + i} = \dfrac{x(2 - i)}{(2 + i)(2 - i)}\]
\[= \dfrac{x(2 - i)}{4 + 1}\]
\[= \dfrac{2x}{5} - \dfrac{x}{5}i\]
Kyun: \(2 + i\) ka conjugate \(2 - i\) hai. Neeche \((2 + i)(2 - i) = 4 - i^2 = 4 + 1 = 5\), jo real number hai. Ab upar \(x(2 - i) = 2x - xi\) hai, aur 5 se divide kar ke hum fraction ko saaf do hisson mein tor sakte hain: real part \(\frac{2x}{5}\) aur imaginary part \(-\frac{x}{5}\).

Doosra fraction rationalise karein
\[\dfrac{y}{3 - i} = \dfrac{y(3 + i)}{(3 - i)(3 + i)}\]
\[= \dfrac{y(3 + i)}{9 + 1}\]
\[= \dfrac{3y}{10} + \dfrac{y}{10}i\]
Kyun: Isi tarah \(3 - i\) ka conjugate \(3 + i\) hai, aur \((3 - i)(3 + i) = 9 - i^2 = 10\). Upar \(3y + yi\) ko 10 se divide kiya to real part \(\frac{3y}{10}\) aur imaginary part \(\frac{y}{10}\) mila.
Dhyan dein: \(4 - i^2\) ko \(4 - 1 = 3\) mat likhiye; \(-i^2 = +1\) hai, is liye jawab 5 aata hai.

Jama kar ke parts compare karein
\[\text{Real: } \dfrac{2x}{5} + \dfrac{3y}{10} = 4\]
\[\text{Imag: } \dfrac{y}{10} - \dfrac{x}{5} = 5\]
Kyun: Dono fractions ko jama karte waqt real parts aapas mein aur imaginary parts aapas mein jurte hain. Yeh jama \(4 + 5i\) ke barabar hai, is liye equality of complex numbers ke mutabiq real parts ka jama 4 aur imaginary parts ka jama 5 hona chahiye. Is tarah do equations mil gayin.

Fractions khatam karein
\[4x + 3y = 40 \quad (1)\]
\[-2x + y = 50 \quad (2)\]
Kyun: Fractions ke saath hisaab mein ghalti ka khatra hota hai. 5 aur 10 ka LCM 10 hai, is liye dono equations ko 10 se multiply kiya: \(\frac{2x}{5} \times 10 = 4x\), \(\frac{3y}{10} \times 10 = 3y\), \(4 \times 10 = 40\). Doosri equation mein \(\frac{y}{10} \times 10 = y\) aur \(-\frac{x}{5} \times 10 = -2x\). Ab poore numbers hain aur kaam aasaan hai.

Dono equations solve karein
\[\text{From (2): } y = 50 + 2x\]
\[4x + 3(50 + 2x) = 40\]
\[10x + 150 = 40\]
\[x = -11\]
\[y = 50 + 2(-11) = 28\]
Kyun: Substitution method use kiya: equation (2) mein \(y\) akela karna sab se aasaan tha, \(y = 50 + 2x\). Isay (1) mein rakha to sirf \(x\) wali equation bachi: \(4x + 150 + 6x = 40\), yani \(10x = -110\), \(x = -11\). Phir \(x\) wapas rakh kar \(y = 50 - 22 = 28\) mila.

Tasdeeq: values wapas rakhein
\[\dfrac{-11}{2 + i} = \dfrac{-22 + 11i}{5}\]
\[\dfrac{28}{3 - i} = \dfrac{42 + 14i}{5}\]
\[\text{Sum} = \dfrac{20 + 25i}{5}\]
\[= 4 + 5i \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(x = -11\) aur \(y = 28\) asal fractions mein rakhe. Pehla fraction \(\frac{-11(2 - i)}{5}\) aur doosra \(\frac{28(3 + i)}{10} = \frac{14(3 + i)}{5}\) bana. Dono ka jama \(\frac{20 + 25i}{5} = 4 + 5i\), bilkul right side. Jawab sahi hai.
blocks.final_answer:
\(x = -11,\ y = 28\)
In values se dono fractions ka jama theek \(4 + 5i\) banta hai.

blocks.prompt: 2 If \(z_1 = -13 + 24i\) and \(z_2 = x + yi\), find the values of \(x\) and \(y\) such that \(z_1 - z_2 = -27 + 15i\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh complex numbers ki subtraction (minus karna) ka sawal hai, jis mein doosra number \(z_2\) humein maloom nahi.
Diya kya hai? \(z_1 = -13 + 24i\), \(z_2 = x + yi\), aur un ka farq \(z_1 - z_2 = -27 + 15i\).
Find kya karna hai? \(z_2\) ke parts, yani \(x\) aur \(y\).
Rule kaunsa? Subtraction mein real ko real se aur imaginary ko imaginary se minus karte hain; phir equality of complex numbers.
Plan: \(z_1 - z_2\) ko \(x, y\) ke saath likhenge, phir \(-27 + 15i\) se compare kar ke do aasaan equations solve karenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(z_1 = -13 + 24i\), \(z_2 = x + yi\), \(z_1 - z_2 = -27 + 15i\).
Humein find karna hai: \(x\) aur \(y\).
Tareeqa: Subtraction ka rule: \((a + ib) - (c + id) = (a - c) + i(b - d)\). Socho do alag dabbe hain, ek real ka aur ek imaginary ka; har cheez apne hi dabbe mein jama ya minus hoti hai. Phir equality of complex numbers se do equations milengi.

\(z_1\) mein se \(z_2\) minus karein
\[z_1 - z_2 = (-13 + 24i) - (x + yi)\]
\[= (-13 - x) + (24 - y)i\]
Kyun: Bracket ke bahar minus ka sign \(z_2\) ke dono parts par lagta hai: \(-(x + yi) = -x - yi\). Phir real parts \(-13\) aur \(-x\) ek saath, aur imaginary parts \(24i\) aur \(-yi\) ek saath likhe.
Dhyan dein: Bohat se students sirf \(x\) par minus lagate hain aur \(yi\) ko plus chhor dete hain. Minus poore bracket par lagta hai.

\(-27 + 15i\) se compare karein
\[-13 - x = -27\]
\[x = 14\]
\[24 - y = 15\]
\[y = 9\]
Kyun: Equality of complex numbers: real part \(-13 - x\) ko real part \(-27\) ke barabar rakha, to \(-x = -27 + 13 = -14\), yani \(x = 14\). Imaginary part \(24 - y = 15\), to \(-y = -9\), yani \(y = 9\).

Tasdeeq
\[(-13 + 24i) - (14 + 9i)\]
\[= -27 + 15i \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(z_2 = 14 + 9i\) lekar \(z_1\) mein se minus kiya: \(-13 - 14 = -27\) aur \(24 - 9 = 15\). Wohi farq mila jo sawal mein diya tha, is liye jawab sahi hai.
blocks.final_answer:
\(x = 14,\ y = 9\) (yani \(z_2 = 14 + 9i\))
Matlab \(z_1\) mein se \(14 + 9i\) nikal dein to \(-27 + 15i\) bachta hai.

blocks.prompt: 3 (i) Find the values of \(x\) and \(y\) if \((x + iy)^2 = 25 + 60i\).
blocks.explanation:
Humein aisa complex number \(x + iy\) chahiye jiska square \(25 + 60i\) ho, yani asal mein yeh square root ka sawal hai, bas shakal badli hui hai.
Diya kya hai? \((x + iy)^2 = 25 + 60i\).
Find kya karna hai? Real numbers \(x\) aur \(y\); do jore milenge, kyunke har complex number ke do square roots hote hain.
Rule kaunsa? Expand kar ke equality of complex numbers, phir \(x^2 + y^2\) wali identity.
Plan: expand, compare, \(x^2 + y^2\) nikalna, jama aur minus, aur aakhir mein \(2xy\) ke sign se sahi jore banana.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \((x + iy)^2 = 25 + 60i\), \(x, y\) real hain.
Humein find karna hai: \(x\) aur \(y\).
Tareeqa: \((x + iy)^2\) ko expand karenge, parts compare karenge, phir identity \((x^2 + y^2)^2 = (x^2 - y^2)^2 + (2xy)^2\) se \(x^2 + y^2\) nikalenge. Jama aur minus karne se \(x^2\) aur \(y^2\) milenge; \(2xy\) ka sign batayega ke kaun se signs saath jayenge. Yeh tareeqa isliye kaam karta hai ke \(x^2 - y^2\) aur \(2xy\) to compare karne se mil jate hain, aur \(x^2 + y^2\) mil jaye to do aasaan equations ban jati hain.

Square ko expand karein
\[(x + iy)^2 = x^2 + 2ixy + i^2y^2\]
\[= (x^2 - y^2) + 2xy\,i\]
Kyun: \((p + q)^2 = p^2 + 2pq + q^2\) wala jaana pehchana formula lagaya, jahan \(q = iy\). Is mein \((iy)^2 = i^2y^2 = -y^2\) ho jata hai, kyunke \(i^2 = -1\). Is liye real part \(x^2 - y^2\) bana aur imaginary part \(2xy\).
Dhyan dein: \((iy)^2\) ko \(+y^2\) likhna sab se aam ghalti hai; isi minus ki wajah se real part \(x^2 - y^2\) hai.

Real aur imaginary parts compare karein
\[x^2 - y^2 = 25 \quad (1)\]
\[2xy = 60 \quad (2)\]
Kyun: Left side ab \(a + ib\) shakal mein hai aur right side bhi. Equality of complex numbers: real se real (equation 1) aur imaginary se imaginary (equation 2). Lekin yeh do equations seedhi solve nahi hotin, is liye agla qadam chahiye.

\(x^2 + y^2\) nikalein
\[(x^2 + y^2)^2 = (x^2 - y^2)^2 + (2xy)^2\]
\[= 25^2 + 60^2\]
\[= 625 + 3600 = 4225\]
\[x^2 + y^2 = 65 \quad (3)\]
Kyun: Yeh identity har number ke liye sahi hai: dono sides expand karein to \(x^4 + 2x^2y^2 + y^4\) hi aata hai. Is ka faida yeh hai ke right side ki dono cheezein humein (1) aur (2) se maloom hain. \(x^2 + y^2\) do squares ka jama hai, kabhi negative nahi ho sakta, is liye sirf positive square root lete hain.

(1) aur (3) jama kar ke \(x\) nikalein
\[2x^2 = 25 + 65 = 90\]
\[x^2 = 45\]
\[x = \pm 3\sqrt{5}\]
Kyun: (1) mein \(-y^2\) aur (3) mein \(+y^2\) hai, jama karne se \(y^2\) cancel ho jata hai aur sirf \(x^2\) bachta hai. Phir 2 se divide kar ke square root liya. Square root lete waqt \(\pm\) dono signs aate hain, kyunke positive aur negative dono ka square ek hi hota hai. Yahan \(\sqrt{45} = \sqrt{9 \times 5} = 3\sqrt{5}\) simplify kiya.

(3) mein se (1) minus kar ke \(y\) nikalein
\[2y^2 = 65 - 25 = 40\]
\[y^2 = 20\]
\[y = \pm 2\sqrt{5}\]
Kyun: Is dafa minus karne se \(x^2\) cancel ho gaya aur sirf \(y^2\) bacha: \((x^2 + y^2) - (x^2 - y^2) = 2y^2\). Phir wohi kaam: 2 se divide aur \(\pm\) ke saath square root.

Signs ka faisla karein
\[2xy = 60\]
\[x = 3\sqrt{5},\ y = 2\sqrt{5}\]
\[\text{or } x = -3\sqrt{5},\ y = -2\sqrt{5}\]
Kyun: \(2xy\) positive hai, aur do numbers ka product tabhi positive hota hai jab dono ka sign ek jaisa ho. Is liye \(x\) positive ho to \(y\) bhi positive, aur \(x\) negative ho to \(y\) bhi negative. Chaar mumkin jore nahi, sirf do sahi jore hain.
Dhyan dein: Agar aap \(x\) positive aur \(y\) negative le lein to square karne par imaginary part ka sign ulta aa jayega; yeh exam ki sab se aam ghalti hai.

Tasdeeq
\[x^2 - y^2 = 45 - 20 = 25 \;\checkmark\]
\[2xy = 2(3\sqrt{5})(2\sqrt{5})\]
\[= 12 \times 5 = 60 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Dono asal equations (1) aur (2) mein values rakh kar dekh liya; dono poori ho gayin, is liye jawab sahi hai. Doosra jora pehle jore ka negative hai, aur negative ka square bhi wohi hota hai, is liye woh bhi sahi hai.
blocks.final_answer:
\(x = 3\sqrt{5},\ y = 2\sqrt{5}\) ya \(x = -3\sqrt{5},\ y = -2\sqrt{5}\)
Yani \(25 + 60i\) ke do square roots \(\pm(3\sqrt{5} + 2\sqrt{5}\,i)\) hain.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ki answer key mein \(x = 9,\ y = 5\) ya \(x = -9,\ y = -5\) likha hai, jo ghalat hai. Khud check kar ke dekhiye: \((9 + 5i)^2 = 81 - 25 + 90i = 56 + 90i\) banta hai, \(25 + 60i\) nahi. Sahi jawab \(x = 3\sqrt{5},\ y = 2\sqrt{5}\) ya \(x = -3\sqrt{5},\ y = -2\sqrt{5}\) hai. Sabaq: jawab ko hamesha square kar ke check kijiye.

blocks.prompt: 3 (ii) Find the values of \(x\) and \(y\) if \((x + iy)^2 = 64 + 48i\).

Yeh bilkul part (i) jaisa sawal hai: aisa \(x + iy\) chahiye jiska square \(64 + 48i\) ho.
Diya kya hai? \((x + iy)^2 = 64 + 48i\).
Find kya karna hai? Dono jore \((x, y)\).
Rule kaunsa? Wohi: expand, equality of complex numbers, aur \(x^2 + y^2\) wali identity.
Plan: parts compare, \(x^2 + y^2\), jama aur minus, phir signs ka faisla. Part (i) ko saamne rakh kar khud bhi try kijiye, phir neeche se milaiye.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \((x + iy)^2 = 64 + 48i\), \(x, y\) real hain.
Humein find karna hai: \(x\) aur \(y\).
Tareeqa: \((x + iy)^2\) ko expand karenge, parts compare karenge, phir identity \((x^2 + y^2)^2 = (x^2 - y^2)^2 + (2xy)^2\) se \(x^2 + y^2\) nikalenge. Jama aur minus karne se \(x^2\) aur \(y^2\) milenge; \(2xy\) ka sign batayega ke kaun se signs saath jayenge. Yeh tareeqa isliye kaam karta hai ke \(x^2 - y^2\) aur \(2xy\) to compare karne se mil jate hain, aur \(x^2 + y^2\) mil jaye to do aasaan equations ban jati hain.

Square ko expand karein
\[(x + iy)^2 = x^2 + 2ixy + i^2y^2\]
\[= (x^2 - y^2) + 2xy\,i\]
Kyun: \((p + q)^2 = p^2 + 2pq + q^2\) wala jaana pehchana formula lagaya, jahan \(q = iy\). Is mein \((iy)^2 = i^2y^2 = -y^2\) ho jata hai, kyunke \(i^2 = -1\). Is liye real part \(x^2 - y^2\) bana aur imaginary part \(2xy\).
Dhyan dein: \((iy)^2\) ko \(+y^2\) likhna sab se aam ghalti hai; isi minus ki wajah se real part \(x^2 - y^2\) hai.

Real aur imaginary parts compare karein
\[x^2 - y^2 = 64 \quad (1)\]
\[2xy = 48 \quad (2)\]
Kyun: Left side ab \(a + ib\) shakal mein hai aur right side bhi. Equality of complex numbers: real se real (equation 1) aur imaginary se imaginary (equation 2). Lekin yeh do equations seedhi solve nahi hotin, is liye agla qadam chahiye.

\(x^2 + y^2\) nikalein
\[(x^2 + y^2)^2 = (x^2 - y^2)^2 + (2xy)^2\]
\[= 64^2 + 48^2\]
\[= 4096 + 2304 = 6400\]
\[x^2 + y^2 = 80 \quad (3)\]
Kyun: Yeh identity har number ke liye sahi hai: dono sides expand karein to \(x^4 + 2x^2y^2 + y^4\) hi aata hai. Is ka faida yeh hai ke right side ki dono cheezein humein (1) aur (2) se maloom hain. \(x^2 + y^2\) do squares ka jama hai, kabhi negative nahi ho sakta, is liye sirf positive square root lete hain.

(1) aur (3) jama kar ke \(x\) nikalein
\[2x^2 = 64 + 80 = 144\]
\[x^2 = 72\]
\[x = \pm 6\sqrt{2}\]
Kyun: (1) mein \(-y^2\) aur (3) mein \(+y^2\) hai, jama karne se \(y^2\) cancel ho jata hai aur sirf \(x^2\) bachta hai. Phir 2 se divide kar ke square root liya. Square root lete waqt \(\pm\) dono signs aate hain, kyunke positive aur negative dono ka square ek hi hota hai. Yahan \(\sqrt{72} = \sqrt{36 \times 2} = 6\sqrt{2}\).

(3) mein se (1) minus kar ke \(y\) nikalein
\[2y^2 = 80 - 64 = 16\]
\[y^2 = 8\]
\[y = \pm 2\sqrt{2}\]
Kyun: Is dafa minus karne se \(x^2\) cancel ho gaya aur sirf \(y^2\) bacha: \((x^2 + y^2) - (x^2 - y^2) = 2y^2\). Phir wohi kaam: 2 se divide aur \(\pm\) ke saath square root.

Signs ka faisla karein
\[2xy = 48\]
\[x = 6\sqrt{2},\ y = 2\sqrt{2}\]
\[\text{or } x = -6\sqrt{2},\ y = -2\sqrt{2}\]
Kyun: \(2xy\) positive hai, aur do numbers ka product tabhi positive hota hai jab dono ka sign ek jaisa ho. Is liye \(x\) positive ho to \(y\) bhi positive, aur \(x\) negative ho to \(y\) bhi negative. Chaar mumkin jore nahi, sirf do sahi jore hain.
Dhyan dein: Agar aap \(x\) positive aur \(y\) negative le lein to square karne par imaginary part ka sign ulta aa jayega; yeh exam ki sab se aam ghalti hai.

Tasdeeq
\[x^2 - y^2 = 72 - 8 = 64 \;\checkmark\]
\[2xy = 2(6\sqrt{2})(2\sqrt{2})\]
\[= 24 \times 2 = 48 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Dono asal equations (1) aur (2) mein values rakh kar dekh liya; dono poori ho gayin, is liye jawab sahi hai. Doosra jora pehle jore ka negative hai, aur negative ka square bhi wohi hota hai, is liye woh bhi sahi hai.
blocks.final_answer:
\(x = 6\sqrt{2},\ y = 2\sqrt{2}\) ya \(x = -6\sqrt{2},\ y = -2\sqrt{2}\)
Yani \(64 + 48i\) ke do square roots \(\pm(6\sqrt{2} + 2\sqrt{2}\,i)\) hain.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key mein \(x = 12,\ y = 2\) ya \(x = -12,\ y = -2\) likha hai, jo ghalat hai: \((12 + 2i)^2 = 144 - 4 + 48i = 140 + 48i\) banta hai, \(64 + 48i\) nahi. Sahi jawab \(x = 6\sqrt{2},\ y = 2\sqrt{2}\) ya \(x = -6\sqrt{2},\ y = -2\sqrt{2}\) hai.

blocks.prompt: 3 (iii) Find the values of \(x\) and \(y\) if \(x + iy = \frac{-2 - 5i}{(1 + 3i)^3}\).
blocks.explanation:
Is dafa \(x + iy\) seedha ek fraction ke barabar diya hai, jis ke neeche \((1 + 3i)\) ka cube (power 3) hai.
Diya kya hai? \(x + iy = \frac{-2 - 5i}{(1 + 3i)^3}\).
Find kya karna hai? Is fraction ko \(a + ib\) shakal mein la kar \(x\) aur \(y\) parhne hain.
Rule kaunsa? Cube ko seedha nahi, do aasaan qadmon mein nikalenge (pehle square, phir ek dafa aur multiply). Phir conjugate se divide.
Plan: \((1 + 3i)^2\), phir \((1 + 3i)^3\), minus signs saaf, conjugate se multiply, aur parts compare.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(x + iy = \frac{-2 - 5i}{(1 + 3i)^3}\).
Humein find karna hai: \(x\) aur \(y\).
Tareeqa: Pehle \((1 + 3i)^2\) nikalenge, phir usay \((1 + 3i)\) se multiply kar ke cube banayenge, kyunke \(z^3 = z^2 \cdot z\). Jab denominator ek simple complex number ban jaye, to upar neeche us ke conjugate se multiply kar ke denominator real karenge aur fraction ko \(a + ib\) mein toreinge.

Cube ke liye ek dafa aur multiply karein
\[(1 + 3i)^3 = (-8 + 6i)(1 + 3i)\]
\[= -8 - 24i + 6i + 18i^2\]
\[= -8 - 18i - 18\]
\[= -26 - 18i\]
Kyun: \(z^3 = z^2 \cdot z\), yani jo square mila usay asal number se ek dafa aur multiply kiya. Term by term: \(-8 \cdot 1 = -8\), \(-8 \cdot 3i = -24i\), \(6i \cdot 1 = 6i\), \(6i \cdot 3i = 18i^2 = -18\). Real: \(-8 - 18 = -26\); imaginary: \(-24i + 6i = -18i\).

Minus signs hatayein
\[x + iy = \dfrac{-2 - 5i}{-26 - 18i}\]
\[= \dfrac{2 + 5i}{26 + 18i}\]
Kyun: Upar aur neeche dono mein sab terms negative hain. Upar neeche dono ko \(-1\) se multiply karne se value wohi rehti hai (jaise \(\frac{-2}{-4} = \frac{2}{4}\)), lekin signs kam ho jate hain aur aage ghalti ka chance kam ho jata hai. Yeh zaroori qadam nahi, bas samajhdari hai.

Conjugate se multiply karein
\[= \dfrac{(2 + 5i)(26 - 18i)}{(26 + 18i)(26 - 18i)}\]
\[\text{Bottom} = 26^2 + 18^2\]
\[= 676 + 324 = 1000\]
Kyun: \(26 + 18i\) ka conjugate \(26 - 18i\) hai. Formula \((a + ib)(a - ib) = a^2 + b^2\) hamesha real number deta hai, kyunke beech wale \(i\) terms cancel ho jate hain aur \(-i^2b^2 = +b^2\) ban jata hai. Isi liye denominator 1000 jaisa saaf real number ban gaya.

\(a + ib\) form mein likh kar compare karein
\[x + iy = \dfrac{142 + 94i}{1000}\]
\[= \dfrac{71}{500} + \dfrac{47}{500}i\]
\[x = \dfrac{71}{500},\quad y = \dfrac{47}{500}\]
Kyun: Denominator real hai, is liye har part ko alag 1000 se divide kar sakte hain. Dono ko 2 se chhota kiya: \(142/1000 = 71/500\), \(94/1000 = 47/500\). Ab equality of complex numbers se real part \(x\) aur imaginary part \(y\) seedha mil gaye.

Tasdeeq: wapas multiply karein
\[(71 + 47i)(-26 - 18i)\]
\[= -1846 - 1278i - 1222i - 846i^2\]
\[= -1000 - 2500i\]
\[\div 500: \; -2 - 5i \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Agar \(x + iy\) sahi hai to \((x + iy)(1 + 3i)^3\) wapas numerator \(-2 - 5i\) dena chahiye. Fractions se bachne ke liye \(500(x + iy) = 71 + 47i\) ko \(-26 - 18i\) se multiply kiya: \(-846i^2 = +846\), real \(-1846 + 846 = -1000\), imaginary \(-2500i\). 500 se divide kiya to \(-2 - 5i\) mila. Jawab sahi hai.
blocks.final_answer:
\(x = \frac{71}{500},\ y = \frac{47}{500}\)
Yani yeh fraction ek chhota sa complex number \(0.142 + 0.094i\) hai.

blocks.prompt: 4 If \(z_1 = 2 + 3i\) and \(z_2 = 1 - \alpha\), find the value of \(\alpha\) such that \(\operatorname{Im}(z_1 z_2) = 7\).
blocks.explanation:
Yahan do complex numbers ka product (multiply) hai jis mein ek unknown real number \(\alpha\) (alpha) chhupa hai.
\(\operatorname{Im}(z_1 z_2)\) ka matlab hai product ka imaginary part, yani \(i\) ke saath wala real number (\(i\) khud nahi).
Ek zaroori baat: kitab mein \(z_2 = 1 - \alpha\) chhapa hai, \(i\) reh gaya hai (neeche "Kitab ki ghalti" dekhein). Kitab ka jawab \(\alpha = -2\) tabhi aata hai jab \(z_2 = 1 - \alpha i\) ho, is liye hum wohi solve karenge aur chhapa hua version bhi dikha denge.
Plan: multiply, real aur imaginary terms alag, imaginary part ko 7 ke barabar rakh kar \(\alpha\) nikalna.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(z_1 = 2 + 3i\), \(z_2 = 1 - \alpha i\) (sahi form; kitab mein \(1 - \alpha\)), \(\alpha\) real, \(\operatorname{Im}(z_1 z_2) = 7\).
Humein find karna hai: \(\alpha\).
Tareeqa: \(z_1 z_2\) ko multiply kar ke (real part) + (imaginary part)\(i\) ki shakal mein likhenge. Phir sirf imaginary part ko 7 ke barabar rakhenge; is se \(\alpha\) ki ek simple linear equation banegi. Real part ki yahan koi shart nahi, woh kuch bhi ho sakta hai.

\(z_1\) aur \(z_2\) multiply karein
\[z_1 z_2 = (2 + 3i)(1 - \alpha i)\]
\[= 2 - 2\alpha i + 3i - 3\alpha i^2\]
\[= 2 - 2\alpha i + 3i + 3\alpha\]
\[= (2 + 3\alpha) + (3 - 2\alpha)i\]
Kyun: Har term ko har term se multiply kiya: \(2 \cdot 1 = 2\), \(2(-\alpha i) = -2\alpha i\), \(3i \cdot 1 = 3i\), \(3i(-\alpha i) = -3\alpha i^2 = +3\alpha\). \(+3\alpha\) mein ab \(i\) nahi raha, is liye woh real part mein jata hai. Phir real terms \(2 + 3\alpha\) ek bracket mein, aur \(i\) wale terms se \(i\) common nikal kar \((3 - 2\alpha)i\).

Imaginary part ko 7 ke barabar rakhein
\[3 - 2\alpha = 7\]
\[-2\alpha = 4\]
\[\alpha = -2\]
Kyun: Imaginary part \(i\) ka coefficient (saath laga hua number) hai, yani \(3 - 2\alpha\). Isay 7 ke barabar rakha, 3 ko doosri taraf le gaye: \(-2\alpha = 4\), phir \(-2\) se divide kiya.
Dhyan dein: Imaginary part mein \(i\) shamil nahi hota. \((3 - 2\alpha)i = 7\) likhna ghalat hai; sahi \(3 - 2\alpha = 7\) hai.

Kitab wala version, muqable ke liye
\[(2 + 3i)(1 - \alpha)\]
\[= 2(1 - \alpha) + 3(1 - \alpha)i\]
\[3(1 - \alpha) = 7\]
\[\alpha = -\dfrac{4}{3}\]
Kyun: Ab dekhte hain agar sawal bilkul waisa hi lein jaisa chhapa hai: \(z_2 = 1 - \alpha\) ek real number hai. Real number se multiply karne par imaginary part \(3(1 - \alpha)\) banta hai. \(3 - 3\alpha = 7\) se \(\alpha = -\frac{4}{3}\) aata hai, key wala \(-2\) nahi. Yahi saboot hai ke chhapai mein \(i\) reh gaya tha. Exam mein agar aisa sawal aaye to apni assumption saaf likh dijiye.

Tasdeeq
\[\alpha = -2: \; z_2 = 1 + 2i\]
\[(2 + 3i)(1 + 2i)\]
\[= 2 + 4i + 3i + 6i^2\]
\[= -4 + 7i\]
\[\operatorname{Im} = 7 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(\alpha = -2\) rakhne se \(z_2 = 1 - (-2)i = 1 + 2i\) bana. Product mein \(6i^2 = -6\), to real part \(2 - 6 = -4\) aur imaginary part \(4 + 3 = 7\). Imaginary part bilkul 7 hai, jaisa chahiye tha.
blocks.final_answer:
\(\alpha = -2\) (\(z_2 = 1 - \alpha i\) ke saath); kitab ke mutabiq \(z_2 = 1 - \alpha\) lein to \(\alpha = -\frac{4}{3}\)
Yani \(z_2 = 1 + 2i\) lene se product \(-4 + 7i\) banta hai, jis ka imaginary part 7 hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein \(z_2 = 1 - \alpha\) chhapa hai. Agar \(\alpha\) real ho to is se \(\operatorname{Im}(z_1 z_2) = 3(1 - \alpha) = 7\), yani \(\alpha = -\frac{4}{3}\) aata hai, jo answer key ke \(\alpha = -2\) se nahi milta. Sahi sawal \(z_2 = 1 - \alpha i\) hai (chhapai mein \(i\) reh gaya); tab \(3 - 2\alpha = 7\) se \(\alpha = -2\) milta hai.

blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein do complex numbers \(z_1\) aur \(z_2\) dono unknown hain, lekin un ka jama (sum) aur farq (difference) diya hua hai.
Find kya karna hai? Chaar real numbers \(x, y, a, b\).
Chaar unknowns ke liye chaar equations chahiye; har complex condition do equations deti hai (ek real, ek imaginary), to do conditions se poori chaar mil jayengi.
Rule kaunsa? Addition aur subtraction part by part, phir equality of complex numbers.
Plan: dono conditions se chaar equations, phir jore bana kar jama karna taake ek ek unknown cancel ho jaye.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(z_1 = x + yi\), \(z_2 = a + bi\), \(z_1 + z_2 = 10 + 4i\), \(z_1 - z_2 = 6 + 2i\).
Humein find karna hai: \(x, y, a, b\).
Tareeqa: Complex numbers ka jama aur minus part by part hota hai: real real ke saath, imaginary imaginary ke saath. Phir equality of complex numbers lagayenge. Equations is tarah jore banati hain ke \(x\) aur \(a\) ki do equations alag hongi aur \(y\) aur \(b\) ki do alag; jama karne se \(a\) ya \(b\) khatam ho jata hai.

Sum wali condition
\[z_1 + z_2 = (x + a) + (y + b)i\]
\[x + a = 10 \quad (1)\]
\[y + b = 4 \quad (2)\]
Kyun: \((x + yi) + (a + bi)\) mein real parts \(x + a\) aur imaginary parts \(y + b\) hain. Isay \(10 + 4i\) se compare kiya: real part 10 ke barabar aur imaginary part 4 ke barabar.

Difference wali condition
\[z_1 - z_2 = (x - a) + (y - b)i\]
\[x - a = 6 \quad (3)\]
\[y - b = 2 \quad (4)\]
Kyun: Minus mein bhi yehi tareeqa: \(-(a + bi) = -a - bi\), to real part \(x - a\) aur imaginary part \(y - b\). \(6 + 2i\) se compare kar ke do aur equations mil gayin. Ab humare paas chaar unknowns ke liye chaar equations hain.

(1) aur (3) solve karein
\[(1) + (3): \; 2x = 16\]
\[x = 8\]
\[a = 10 - 8 = 2\]
Kyun: (1) mein \(+a\) aur (3) mein \(-a\) hai; jama karne se \(a\) cancel ho gaya aur \(2x = 16\) bacha. Isay elimination method kehte hain. Phir \(x = 8\) ko (1) mein rakha: \(8 + a = 10\), to \(a = 2\).

(2) aur (4) solve karein
\[(2) + (4): \; 2y = 6\]
\[y = 3\]
\[b = 4 - 3 = 1\]
Kyun: Bilkul wohi chaal: (2) aur (4) jama karne se \(b\) cancel hua, \(2y = 6\), \(y = 3\). Phir (2) mein rakha: \(3 + b = 4\), to \(b = 1\).

Tasdeeq
\[(8 + 3i) + (2 + i) = 10 + 4i \;\checkmark\]
\[(8 + 3i) - (2 + i) = 6 + 2i \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(z_1 = 8 + 3i\) aur \(z_2 = 2 + i\) bane. Dono ka jama \(10 + 4i\) aur farq \(6 + 2i\) hai, yani dono di gayi conditions poori ho gayin. Jawab sahi hai.
blocks.final_answer:
\(x = 8,\ y = 3,\ a = 2,\ b = 1\) (yani \(z_1 = 8 + 3i\), \(z_2 = 2 + i\))
Yani yeh do numbers aise hain jin ka jama \(10 + 4i\) aur farq \(6 + 2i\) hai.

blocks.prompt: 6 Show that \(\forall\, z_1, z_2 \in C\), \(\overline{z_1 z_2} = \overline{z_1}\,\overline{z_2}\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh proof (saboot) wala sawal hai. Symbol \(\forall\) ka matlab hai "har ek ke liye", yani baat har do complex numbers ke liye sahi saabit karni hai.
Is liye hum khaas numbers (jaise \(2 + 3i\)) nahi lete, balkay letters lete hain jo kisi bhi number ki jagah ho sakte hain.
Saabit kya karna hai? Product ka conjugate = conjugates ka product. Conjugate ko aise samjhiye jaise real axis mein aaina (mirror image): sirf \(i\) wale part ka sign ulat jata hai.
Plan: \(z_1 = a + ib\), \(z_2 = c + id\) likhenge; left side (pehle multiply, phir conjugate) aur right side (pehle conjugate, phir multiply) alag alag nikal kar dikhayenge ke dono bilkul ek hain.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(z_1, z_2\) koi bhi complex numbers hain.
Humein find karna hai: saabit karna hai ke \(\overline{z_1 z_2} = \overline{z_1}\,\overline{z_2}\).
Tareeqa: \(z_1 = a + ib\), \(z_2 = c + id\) lenge, jahan \(a, b, c, d\) real hain. Proof mein dono sides ko alag alag hal karte hain aur kabhi ek side ko doosri side mein "maan" kar shuru nahi karte. Left side: pehle multiply, phir conjugate. Right side: pehle conjugate, phir multiply. Aakhir mein compare.

\(z_1\) aur \(z_2\) multiply karein
\[z_1 z_2 = (a + ib)(c + id)\]
\[= ac + iad + ibc + i^2 bd\]
\[= (ac - bd) + i(ad + bc)\]
Kyun: Left side ke liye pehle product chahiye. Term by term multiply kiya: \(a \cdot c\), \(a \cdot id\), \(ib \cdot c\), \(ib \cdot id = i^2 bd = -bd\). Real terms \(ac - bd\) ek saath, aur \(i\) wale terms se \(i\) common nikal kar \(i(ad + bc)\). Yeh complex numbers ke product ka general formula hai, aage bhi kaam aayega.

Left side: product ka conjugate
\[\overline{z_1 z_2} = (ac - bd) - i(ad + bc)\]
Kyun: Conjugate lene ka rule: real part wahi rehta hai, sirf imaginary part ka sign ulat jata hai. Is liye \(+i(ad + bc)\) ban gaya \(-i(ad + bc)\), aur \(ac - bd\) waisa hi raha.
Dhyan dein: Real part ke andar wale minus (\(-bd\)) ko mat chheriye; conjugate sirf \(i\) wale hisse ko badalta hai.

Right side: conjugates ka product
\[\overline{z_1} = a - ib, \quad \overline{z_2} = c - id\]
\[\overline{z_1}\,\overline{z_2} = (a - ib)(c - id)\]
\[= ac - iad - ibc + i^2 bd\]
\[= (ac - bd) - i(ad + bc)\]
Kyun: Ab ulti tarteeb: pehle har number ka conjugate liya, phir multiply kiya. \((-ib)(-id)\) mein do minus milkar plus bante hain: \(+i^2bd = -bd\). Baqi do terms \(-iad - ibc\) se \(-i\) common nikala to \(-i(ad + bc)\) mila.

Dono sides compare karein
\[\overline{z_1 z_2} = (ac - bd) - i(ad + bc)\]
\[\overline{z_1}\,\overline{z_2} = (ac - bd) - i(ad + bc)\]
Kyun: Dono sides ka real part \(ac - bd\) hai aur imaginary part \(-(ad + bc)\) hai, yani dono bilkul ek hi complex number hain. Kyunke \(a, b, c, d\) koi bhi real numbers ho sakte the, yeh nateeja har \(z_1, z_2\) ke liye sahi hai, aur yahi proof ka matlab hai.

Numbers se tasdeeq
\[z_1 = 1 + 2i,\; z_2 = 3 - i\]
\[z_1 z_2 = 5 + 5i\]
\[\overline{z_1 z_2} = 5 - 5i\]
\[(1 - 2i)(3 + i) = 5 - 5i \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Hamari taraf se ek chhoti si misaal: \((1 + 2i)(3 - i) = 3 - i + 6i - 2i^2 = 5 + 5i\), jis ka conjugate \(5 - 5i\). Doosri taraf \((1 - 2i)(3 + i) = 3 + i - 6i - 2i^2 = 5 - 5i\). Dono barabar. Yaad rakhiye, sirf ek misaal proof nahi hoti; proof upar wali letters wali algebra hai, misaal sirf tasdeeq hai.
blocks.final_answer:
Saabit ho gaya: har \(z_1, z_2 \in C\) ke liye \(\overline{z_1 z_2} = \overline{z_1}\,\overline{z_2}\).
Matlab pehle multiply kar ke conjugate lein ya pehle conjugate le kar multiply karein, nateeja ek hi aata hai.

blocks.prompt: 7 (i) Find the square root of the complex number \(-7 - 24i\).
blocks.explanation:
Humein woh do complex numbers chahiye jinka square \(-7 - 24i\) ho. Har non-zero complex number ke bilkul do square roots hote hain, aur dono ek doosre ke negative hote hain.
Diya kya hai? \(z = -7 - 24i\), yani \(x = -7\), \(y = -24\).
Rule kaunsa? Section 1.2.1 ka square root formula, jo \(|z|\), \(p\) aur \(q\) se kaam karta hai.
Plan: pehle \(|z|\), phir \(p\) aur \(q\), phir \(y\) ke sign se signs ka faisla, aur aakhir mein square kar ke check.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(z = -7 - 24i\).
Humein find karna hai: \(\sqrt{z}\), dono square roots.
Tareeqa: Square root ka formula (Section 1.2.1): \(p = \sqrt{\frac{|z| + x}{2}}\), \(q = \sqrt{\frac{|z| - x}{2}}\); agar \(y > 0\) ho to \(\sqrt{z} = \pm(p + iq)\), aur \(y < 0\) ho to \(\pm(p - iq)\). Yeh formula kisi bhi \(x + iy\) ke dono square roots seedha de deta hai, is liye har dafa \((a + ib)^2\) expand kar ke equations banane ki zaroorat nahi. Sirf teen cheezein chahiye: \(x\), \(y\) ka sign, aur \(|z|\).

\(x\) aur \(y\) parhein
\[x = -7,\quad y = -24 < 0\]
Kyun: Pehle number ko \(x + iy\) shakal mein dekh kar real part \(x\) aur imaginary part \(y\) pehchante hain. \(x\) formula mein jayega, aur \(y\) ka sign aakhir mein yeh tay karega ke jawab ke dono hisson ke signs ek jaise honge ya ulte. Is liye \(y\) ka sign abhi se note kar lein.

Modulus \(|z|\) nikalein
\[|z| = \sqrt{(-7)^2 + (-24)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{49 + 576}\]
\[= \sqrt{625} = 25\]
Kyun: Modulus \(|z| = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}\) number ki origin se doori hai (jaise naqshe par ghar se school ka seedha faasla). Yeh \(p\) aur \(q\) dono ke formula mein chahiye, is liye pehle isay nikalte hain. Squares lene se minus khatam ho jata hai, is liye modulus hamesha positive hota hai.

\(p\) nikalein
\[p = \sqrt{\dfrac{25 + (-7)}{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{9} = 3\]
Kyun: \(|z|\) aur \(x\) ko \(p = \sqrt{(|z| + x)/2}\) mein rakha. \(p\) jawab ka real part hai. \(25 - 7 = 18\), aur \(18/2 = 9\).
Dhyan dein: \(x\) negative hai, is liye \(|z| + x\) mein asal mein minus hota hai aur \(|z| - x\) mein plus. Bracket laga kar likhiye taake sign ki ghalti na ho.

\(q\) nikalein
\[q = \sqrt{\dfrac{25 - (-7)}{2}}\]

blocks.prompt: 9 Find the value of \(x\) and \(y\) if \((-7 + i)(x + iy) + (-1 - 5i) = i(11 - i)\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh ek equation hai jis mein unknown complex number \(x + iy\) ek complex number \((-7 + i)\) se multiply ho kar aaya hai, aur saath ek constant bhi jura hai.
Diya kya hai? \((-7 + i)(x + iy) + (-1 - 5i) = i(11 - i)\).
Find kya karna hai? Real numbers \(x\) aur \(y\).
Rule kaunsa? Jaise aam algebra mein \(3x + 5 = 11\) mein pehle 5 ko doosri taraf le jate hain, waise hi yahan constant ko right side le jayenge; phir expand kar ke equality of complex numbers.
Plan: right side simplify, constant ko right side, left side expand, parts compare, aur do linear equations solve.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \((-7 + i)(x + iy) + (-1 - 5i) = i(11 - i)\), \(x, y\) real hain.
Humein find karna hai: \(x\) aur \(y\).
Tareeqa: Dono sides ko (real) + (imaginary)\(i\) shakal mein layenge. Phir equality of complex numbers se do simultaneous linear equations milengi, jinhein substitution se solve karenge. (Doosra raasta: \(2 + 16i\) ko \(-7 + i\) se divide karna; dono se ek hi jawab aata hai.)

Right side simplify karein
\[i(11 - i) = 11i - i^2\]
\[= 1 + 11i\]
Kyun: \(i\) ko bracket ke dono terms se multiply kiya: \(11i\) aur \(-i^2\). Kyunke \(i^2 = -1\), \(-i^2 = +1\). Real part pehle likha: \(1 + 11i\).

Constant ko right side le jayein
\[(-7 + i)(x + iy) = 1 + 11i + 1 + 5i\]
\[= 2 + 16i\]
Kyun: Left side par \((-1 - 5i)\) jama ho raha hai; isay hatane ke liye dono sides se \((-1 - 5i)\) minus kiya. Minus karna \(1 + 5i\) jama karne ke barabar hai. Phir real \(1 + 1 = 2\) aur imaginary \(11i + 5i = 16i\).
Dhyan dein: Doosri taraf le jate waqt dono parts ka sign badalta hai; aksar students sirf \(-1\) ka sign badalte hain aur \(-5i\) bhool jate hain.

Left side expand karein
\[(-7 + i)(x + iy)\]
\[= -7x - 7iy + ix + i^2 y\]
\[= (-7x - y) + (x - 7y)i\]
Kyun: Term by term multiply kiya: \(-7 \cdot x\), \(-7 \cdot iy\), \(i \cdot x\), \(i \cdot iy = i^2 y = -y\). \(-y\) mein ab \(i\) nahi raha, is liye woh real part mein \(-7x\) ke saath gaya. \(i\) wale terms \(ix - 7iy\) se \(i\) common: \((x - 7y)i\).

Parts compare karein
\[-7x - y = 2 \quad (1)\]
\[x - 7y = 16 \quad (2)\]
Kyun: Ab left side \((-7x - y) + (x - 7y)i\) aur right side \(2 + 16i\) hai. Equality of complex numbers: real se real (1), imaginary se imaginary (2). Do unknowns, do equations, ab aam algebra hai.

Equations solve karein
\[\text{From (1): } y = -7x - 2\]
\[x - 7(-7x - 2) = 16\]
\[50x + 14 = 16\]
\[x = \dfrac{2}{50} = \dfrac{1}{25}\]
\[y = -\dfrac{7}{25} - 2 = -\dfrac{57}{25}\]
Kyun: (1) se \(y\) akela karna aasaan tha: \(y = -7x - 2\). Isay (2) mein rakha: \(x + 49x + 14 = 16\), yani \(50x = 2\), \(x = \frac{1}{25}\). Phir \(y = -\frac{7}{25} - \frac{50}{25} = -\frac{57}{25}\).
Dhyan dein: \(-7(-7x - 2)\) kholte waqt dono terms plus bante hain: \(+49x + 14\).

Tasdeeq
\[(-7 + i)(1 - 57i)\]
\[= -7 + 399i + i - 57i^2\]
\[= 50 + 400i\]
\[\div 25: \; 2 + 16i \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(x + iy = \frac{1 - 57i}{25}\) hai. Fractions se bachne ke liye pehle \(1 - 57i\) ko \(-7 + i\) se multiply kiya: \(-57i^2 = +57\), real \(-7 + 57 = 50\), imaginary \(399i + i = 400i\). Phir 25 se divide kiya to \(2 + 16i\) mila, jo step 3 ka right side hai. Jawab sahi hai.

\(x = \frac{1}{25},\ y = -\frac{57}{25}\)

blocks.prompt: 10 Find the value of \(x\) and \(y\) if \((5 - 2i)(x + iy) + 3 = i(11 - i) - 4i\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh bilkul Question 9 jaisa sawal hai, bas numbers alag hain aur is dafa constant 3 ek real number hai.
Diya kya hai? \((5 - 2i)(x + iy) + 3 = i(11 - i) - 4i\).
Find kya karna hai? Real numbers \(x\) aur \(y\).
Rule kaunsa? Simplify, constant ko doosri taraf, expand, aur equality of complex numbers.
Plan: right side simplify, 3 ko doosri taraf, expand, parts compare, aur is dafa elimination method se solve (taake aap dono tareeqe dekh lein).
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \((5 - 2i)(x + iy) + 3 = i(11 - i) - 4i\), \(x, y\) real hain.
Humein find karna hai: \(x\) aur \(y\).
Tareeqa: Dono sides ko (real) + (imaginary)\(i\) shakal mein la kar parts compare karenge. Jo do linear equations banengi un mein fractions aate hain, is liye elimination method (ek variable ko jama ya minus se khatam karna) yahan zyada saaf rahega.

Right side simplify karein
\[i(11 - i) - 4i = 11i - i^2 - 4i\]
\[= 1 + 7i\]
Kyun: \(i(11 - i) = 11i - i^2\), aur \(-i^2 = +1\). Phir \(i\) wale terms \(11i - 4i = 7i\) jama kiye.

3 ko right side le jayein
\[(5 - 2i)(x + iy) = 1 + 7i - 3\]
\[= -2 + 7i\]
Kyun: Dono sides se 3 minus kiya. 3 real number hai, is liye sirf real part badla: \(1 - 3 = -2\), imaginary part \(7i\) waisa hi raha.

Left side expand karein
\[(5 - 2i)(x + iy)\]
\[= 5x + 5iy - 2ix - 2i^2 y\]
\[= (5x + 2y) + (5y - 2x)i\]
Kyun: Term by term: \(5x\), \(5iy\), \(-2ix\), aur \(-2i \cdot iy = -2i^2y = +2y\). \(+2y\) real hai, \(5x\) ke saath real part mein gaya; \(i\) wale terms se \((5y - 2x)i\).
Dhyan dein: \(-2i^2y\) ka sign plus banta hai; isay \(-2y\) likhne se poora jawab ghalat ho jayega.

Parts compare karein
\[5x + 2y = -2 \quad (1)\]
\[-2x + 5y = 7 \quad (2)\]
Kyun: Equality of complex numbers: real part \(5x + 2y\) ko \(-2\) ke barabar aur imaginary part \(5y - 2x\) ko 7 ke barabar rakha. Equation (2) mein \(x\) ko pehle likha taake dono equations ek jaisi tarteeb mein hon.

\(x\) ko eliminate karein
\[2 \times (1): \; 10x + 4y = -4\]
\[5 \times (2): \; -10x + 25y = 35\]
\[\text{Add: } 29y = 31\]
\[y = \dfrac{31}{29}\]
Kyun: Hum chahte hain ke \(x\) khatam ho jaye. (1) mein \(x\) ka coefficient 5 aur (2) mein \(-2\) hai. (1) ko 2 se aur (2) ko 5 se multiply kiya to coefficients \(10\) aur \(-10\) ban gaye; jama karne par \(x\) cancel aur \(4y + 25y = 29y\), \(-4 + 35 = 31\).

Tasdeeq
\[(5 - 2i)(-24 + 31i)\]
\[= -120 + 155i + 48i - 62i^2\]
\[= -58 + 203i\]
\[\div 29: \; -2 + 7i \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(x + iy = \frac{-24 + 31i}{29}\). Pehle \(-24 + 31i\) ko \(5 - 2i\) se multiply kiya: \(-62i^2 = +62\), real \(-120 + 62 = -58\), imaginary \(155i + 48i = 203i\). 29 se divide kiya to \(-2 + 7i\) mila, jo step 3 ka right side hai.

blocks.prompt: 11 (i) Find the values of \(u\) and \(v\) if \((u + iv)^2 = 20 + 21i\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh Question 3 wala hi sawal hai, bas \(x, y\) ki jagah letters \(u, v\) hain. Letters badalne se tareeqa nahi badalta.
Diya kya hai? \((u + iv)^2 = 20 + 21i\).
Find kya karna hai? \(u\) aur \(v\); do jore milenge.
Rule kaunsa? Expand, equality of complex numbers, aur \(u^2 + v^2\) wali identity.
Plan: parts compare, \(u^2 + v^2\), jama aur minus, phir \(2uv\) ke sign se jore. Kitab ki answer key mein is sawal ka jawab hai hi nahi, is liye tasdeeq zaroor kijiye.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \((u + iv)^2 = 20 + 21i\), \(u, v\) real hain.
Humein find karna hai: \(u\) aur \(v\).
Tareeqa: \((u + iv)^2\) ko expand karenge, parts compare karenge, phir identity \((u^2 + v^2)^2 = (u^2 - v^2)^2 + (2uv)^2\) se \(u^2 + v^2\) nikalenge. Jama aur minus karne se \(u^2\) aur \(v^2\) milenge; \(2uv\) ka sign batayega ke kaun se signs saath jayenge. Yeh tareeqa isliye kaam karta hai ke \(u^2 - v^2\) aur \(2uv\) to compare karne se mil jate hain, aur \(u^2 + v^2\) mil jaye to do aasaan equations ban jati hain.

Square ko expand karein
\[(u + iv)^2 = u^2 + 2iuv + i^2v^2\]
\[= (u^2 - v^2) + 2uv\,i\]
Kyun: \((p + q)^2 = p^2 + 2pq + q^2\) wala jaana pehchana formula lagaya, jahan \(q = iv\). Is mein \((iv)^2 = i^2v^2 = -v^2\) ho jata hai, kyunke \(i^2 = -1\). Is liye real part \(u^2 - v^2\) bana aur imaginary part \(2uv\).
Dhyan dein: \((iv)^2\) ko \(+v^2\) likhna sab se aam ghalti hai; isi minus ki wajah se real part \(u^2 - v^2\) hai.

Real aur imaginary parts compare karein
\[u^2 - v^2 = 20 \quad (1)\]
\[2uv = 21 \quad (2)\]
Kyun: Left side ab \(a + ib\) shakal mein hai aur right side bhi. Equality of complex numbers: real se real (equation 1) aur imaginary se imaginary (equation 2). Lekin yeh do equations seedhi solve nahi hotin, is liye agla qadam chahiye.

\(u^2 + v^2\) nikalein
\[(u^2 + v^2)^2 = (u^2 - v^2)^2 + (2uv)^2\]
\[= 20^2 + 21^2\]
\[= 400 + 441 = 841\]
\[u^2 + v^2 = 29 \quad (3)\]
Kyun: Yeh identity har number ke liye sahi hai: dono sides expand karein to \(u^4 + 2u^2v^2 + v^4\) hi aata hai. Is ka faida yeh hai ke right side ki dono cheezein humein (1) aur (2) se maloom hain. \(u^2 + v^2\) do squares ka jama hai, kabhi negative nahi ho sakta, is liye sirf positive square root lete hain.

(1) aur (3) jama kar ke \(u\) nikalein
\[2u^2 = 20 + 29 = 49\]
\[u^2 = \dfrac{49}{2}\]
\[u = \pm\dfrac{7}{\sqrt{2}} = \pm\dfrac{7\sqrt{2}}{2}\]
Kyun: (1) mein \(-v^2\) aur (3) mein \(+v^2\) hai, jama karne se \(v^2\) cancel ho jata hai aur sirf \(u^2\) bachta hai. Phir 2 se divide kar ke square root liya. Square root lete waqt \(\pm\) dono signs aate hain, kyunke positive aur negative dono ka square ek hi hota hai. \(\frac{7}{\sqrt{2}}\) ko upar neeche \(\sqrt{2}\) se multiply kar ke \(\frac{7\sqrt{2}}{2}\) likha, taake denominator mein root na rahe (rationalise karna).

(3) mein se (1) minus kar ke \(v\) nikalein
\[2v^2 = 29 - 20 = 9\]
\[v^2 = \dfrac{9}{2}\]
\[v = \pm\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{2}} = \pm\dfrac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}\]
Kyun: Is dafa minus karne se \(u^2\) cancel ho gaya aur sirf \(v^2\) bacha: \((u^2 + v^2) - (u^2 - v^2) = 2v^2\). Phir wohi kaam: 2 se divide aur \(\pm\) ke saath square root.

Signs ka faisla karein
\[2uv = 21\]
\[u = \dfrac{7\sqrt{2}}{2},\ v = \dfrac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}\]
\[\text{or } u = -\dfrac{7\sqrt{2}}{2},\ v = -\dfrac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}\]
Kyun: \(2uv\) positive hai, aur do numbers ka product tabhi positive hota hai jab dono ka sign ek jaisa ho. Is liye \(u\) positive ho to \(v\) bhi positive, aur \(u\) negative ho to \(v\) bhi negative. Chaar mumkin jore nahi, sirf do sahi jore hain.
Dhyan dein: Agar aap \(u\) positive aur \(v\) negative le lein to square karne par imaginary part ka sign ulta aa jayega; yeh exam ki sab se aam ghalti hai.

Tasdeeq
\[u^2 - v^2 = \dfrac{49}{2} - \dfrac{9}{2} = 20 \;\checkmark\]
\[2uv = 2 \cdot \dfrac{7}{\sqrt{2}} \cdot \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{2}}\]
\[= 2 \cdot \dfrac{21}{2} = 21 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Dono asal equations (1) aur (2) mein values rakh kar dekh liya; dono poori ho gayin, is liye jawab sahi hai. Doosra jora pehle jore ka negative hai, aur negative ka square bhi wohi hota hai, is liye woh bhi sahi hai.
blocks.final_answer:
\(u = \frac{7\sqrt{2}}{2},\ v = \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}\) ya \(u = -\frac{7\sqrt{2}}{2},\ v = -\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}\)
Yani \(20 + 21i\) ke do square roots \(\pm\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(7 + 3i)\) hain.

blocks.prompt: 11 (ii) Find the values of \(u\) and \(v\) if \((u + iv)^2 = 48 - 10i\).
blocks.explanation:
Part (i) wala hi tareeqa hai, lekin is dafa numbers perfect squares nahi nikalte, is liye jawab mein root ke andar root (nested root) aayega. Yeh normal hai, ghalti nahi.
Diya kya hai? \((u + iv)^2 = 48 - 10i\); dhyan dein imaginary part negative hai.
Find kya karna hai? \(u\) aur \(v\).
Rule kaunsa? Wohi: expand, compare, \(u^2 + v^2\) wali identity.
Plan: parts compare, \(u^2 + v^2\), jama aur minus; \(2uv\) negative hai is liye signs ulte honge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \((u + iv)^2 = 48 - 10i\), \(u, v\) real hain.
Humein find karna hai: \(u\) aur \(v\).
Tareeqa: \((u + iv)^2\) ko expand karenge, parts compare karenge, phir identity \((u^2 + v^2)^2 = (u^2 - v^2)^2 + (2uv)^2\) se \(u^2 + v^2\) nikalenge. Jama aur minus karne se \(u^2\) aur \(v^2\) milenge; \(2uv\) ka sign batayega ke kaun se signs saath jayenge. Yeh tareeqa isliye kaam karta hai ke \(u^2 - v^2\) aur \(2uv\) to compare karne se mil jate hain, aur \(u^2 + v^2\) mil jaye to do aasaan equations ban jati hain.

Square ko expand karein
\[(u + iv)^2 = u^2 + 2iuv + i^2v^2\]
\[= (u^2 - v^2) + 2uv\,i\]
Kyun: \((p + q)^2 = p^2 + 2pq + q^2\) wala jaana pehchana formula lagaya, jahan \(q = iv\). Is mein \((iv)^2 = i^2v^2 = -v^2\) ho jata hai, kyunke \(i^2 = -1\). Is liye real part \(u^2 - v^2\) bana aur imaginary part \(2uv\).
Dhyan dein: \((iv)^2\) ko \(+v^2\) likhna sab se aam ghalti hai; isi minus ki wajah se real part \(u^2 - v^2\) hai.

Real aur imaginary parts compare karein
\[u^2 - v^2 = 48 \quad (1)\]
\[2uv = -10 \quad (2)\]
Kyun: Left side ab \(a + ib\) shakal mein hai aur right side bhi. Equality of complex numbers: real se real (equation 1) aur imaginary se imaginary (equation 2). Lekin yeh do equations seedhi solve nahi hotin, is liye agla qadam chahiye.

\(u^2 + v^2\) nikalein
\[(u^2 + v^2)^2 = (u^2 - v^2)^2 + (2uv)^2\]
\[= 48^2 + (-10)^2\]
\[= 2304 + 100 = 2404\]
\[\sqrt{2404} = \sqrt{4 \times 601} = 2\sqrt{601}\]
\[u^2 + v^2 = 2\sqrt{601} \quad (3)\]
Kyun: Yeh identity har number ke liye sahi hai: dono sides expand karein to \(u^4 + 2u^2v^2 + v^4\) hi aata hai. Is ka faida yeh hai ke right side ki dono cheezein humein (1) aur (2) se maloom hain. \(u^2 + v^2\) do squares ka jama hai, kabhi negative nahi ho sakta, is liye sirf positive square root lete hain.
Dhyan dein: 2404 perfect square nahi, is liye \(2404 = 4 \times 601\) likh kar \(2\sqrt{601}\) banaya; 601 ka aage koi square factor nahi. Aur \((-10)^2 = +100\) hai, minus square mein khatam ho jata hai.

(1) aur (3) jama kar ke \(u\) nikalein
\[2u^2 = 48 + 2\sqrt{601}\]
\[u^2 = 24 + \sqrt{601}\]
\[u = \pm\sqrt{24 + \sqrt{601}}\]
Kyun: (1) mein \(-v^2\) aur (3) mein \(+v^2\) hai, jama karne se \(v^2\) cancel ho jata hai aur sirf \(u^2\) bachta hai. Phir 2 se divide kar ke square root liya. Square root lete waqt \(\pm\) dono signs aate hain, kyunke positive aur negative dono ka square ek hi hota hai. Yahan jawab ko aur simple nahi kar sakte, is liye root ke andar root hi rehne dein.

(3) mein se (1) minus kar ke \(v\) nikalein
\[2v^2 = 2\sqrt{601} - 48\]
\[v^2 = \sqrt{601} - 24\]
\[v = \pm\sqrt{\sqrt{601} - 24}\]
Kyun: Is dafa minus karne se \(u^2\) cancel ho gaya aur sirf \(v^2\) bacha: \((u^2 + v^2) - (u^2 - v^2) = 2v^2\). Phir wohi kaam: 2 se divide aur \(\pm\) ke saath square root.

Signs ka faisla karein
\[2uv = -10\]
\[u = \sqrt{24 + \sqrt{601}}\]
\[v = -\sqrt{\sqrt{601} - 24}\]
\[\text{or the same with signs swapped}\]
\[u \approx \pm 6.97,\quad v \approx \mp 0.72\]
Kyun: Is dafa \(2uv = -10\) negative hai, aur do numbers ka product tabhi negative hota hai jab un ke signs ulte hon. Is liye \(u\) positive ho to \(v\) negative, aur \(u\) negative ho to \(v\) positive. Decimal values (\(\sqrt{601} \approx 24.52\)) se andaaza bhi ho jata hai ke jawab kitna bara hai.
Dhyan dein: Part (i) mein signs ek jaise the, yahan ulte hain; har sawal mein \(2uv\) ka sign khud dekhiye, ratta mat lagaiye.

Tasdeeq
\[u^2 - v^2 = (24 + \sqrt{601}) - (\sqrt{601} - 24)\]
\[= 48 \;\checkmark\]
\[uv = -\sqrt{(\sqrt{601} + 24)(\sqrt{601} - 24)}\]
\[= -\sqrt{601 - 576} = -5\]
\[2uv = -10 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(uv\) ke liye do roots ko ek root mein jora aur \((a + b)(a - b) = a^2 - b^2\) lagaya: \(601 - 24^2 = 601 - 576 = 25\). Dono asal equations (1) aur (2) mein values rakh kar dekh liya; dono poori ho gayin, is liye jawab sahi hai. Doosra jora pehle jore ka negative hai, aur negative ka square bhi wohi hota hai, is liye woh bhi sahi hai.
blocks.final_answer:
\(u = \sqrt{24 + \sqrt{601}},\ v = -\sqrt{\sqrt{601} - 24}\) ya \(u = -\sqrt{24 + \sqrt{601}},\ v = \sqrt{\sqrt{601} - 24}\) (taqreeban \(u \approx \pm 6.97\), \(v \approx \mp 0.72\))
Yani dono roots mein real aur imaginary part ke signs ulte hain, kyunke \(48 - 10i\) ka imaginary part negative hai.

blocks.prompt: 12 If \(z_1 = 4 + 5i\) and \(z_2 = \alpha - 2i\), find the value of \(\alpha\) such that \(\operatorname{Re}(z_1 z_2) = 20\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh Question 4 jaisa sawal hai, lekin is dafa shart (condition) product ke real part par hai.
\(\operatorname{Re}(z_1 z_2)\) product ka woh hissa hai jis ke saath \(i\) nahi laga.
Diya kya hai? \(z_1 = 4 + 5i\), \(z_2 = \alpha - 2i\), aur \(\alpha\) ek unknown real number hai.
Plan: dono ko multiply karenge, real aur imaginary terms alag karenge, real part ko 20 ke barabar rakh kar \(\alpha\) nikalenge. Imaginary part kuch bhi aaye, us ki koi shart nahi.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(z_1 = 4 + 5i\), \(z_2 = \alpha - 2i\), \(\alpha\) real, \(\operatorname{Re}(z_1 z_2) = 20\).
Humein find karna hai: \(\alpha\).
Tareeqa: Dono numbers multiply kar ke product ko (real part) + (imaginary part)\(i\) shakal mein likhenge. Real part \(\alpha\) ki ek linear equation dega, jisay 20 ke barabar rakh kar solve karenge.

\(z_1\) aur \(z_2\) multiply karein
\[z_1 z_2 = (4 + 5i)(\alpha - 2i)\]
\[= 4\alpha - 8i + 5\alpha i - 10i^2\]
\[= (4\alpha + 10) + (5\alpha - 8)i\]
Kyun: Term by term: \(4\alpha\), \(4(-2i) = -8i\), \(5i \cdot \alpha = 5\alpha i\), \(5i(-2i) = -10i^2 = +10\). \(+10\) real hai, is liye \(4\alpha\) ke saath real part mein gaya; \(i\) wale terms \(-8i + 5\alpha i = (5\alpha - 8)i\).
Dhyan dein: Bachche aksar \(-10i^2\) ko imaginary part mein daal dete hain. \(i^2\) real number \(-1\) hai, is liye yeh term real hai.

Real part ko 20 ke barabar rakhein
\[4\alpha + 10 = 20\]
\[4\alpha = 10\]
\[\alpha = \dfrac{10}{4} = \dfrac{5}{2}\]
Kyun: Real part woh term hai jis ke saath \(i\) nahi, yani \(4\alpha + 10\). Isay 20 ke barabar rakha, 10 doosri taraf le gaye: \(4\alpha = 10\), phir 4 se divide kar ke chhota kiya: \(\alpha = \frac{5}{2}\).

Tasdeeq
\[z_2 = \dfrac{5}{2} - 2i\]
\[z_1 z_2 = 20 + \dfrac{9}{2}i\]
\[\operatorname{Re}(z_1 z_2) = 20 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(\alpha = \frac{5}{2}\) rakhne par real part \(4 \cdot \frac{5}{2} + 10 = 10 + 10 = 20\) aur imaginary part \(5 \cdot \frac{5}{2} - 8 = \frac{25}{2} - \frac{16}{2} = \frac{9}{2}\). Real part bilkul 20 hai, jaisa chahiye tha.
blocks.final_answer:
\(\alpha = \frac{5}{2}\)
Yani \(z_2 = \frac{5}{2} - 2i\) lene se product ka real part theek 20 banta hai.
